newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt issuers may pause after sell-off.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt issuers may pause after sell-off.

text.p: Opportunistic issuers of investment-grade corporate bonds in the U.S. may pause following last Friday's sell-off in the Treasury market, syndicate officials said.

But junk bond issuers, who are less sensitive to interest rates fluctuations, are expected to continue to tap the market in droves. Around 20 corporations are expected to tap the market for a total of around $2.5 billion in high-yield debt.
In high-grades, Raytheon Co is seen pricing on Wednesday or Thursday its long-awaited $2.5 billion multi-tranche debt offering, market sources said.
"What was (previously) scheduled for this week will be issued," said one high-grade syndicate official. "But issuers who were on the fence are probably going to hold off now."

Last Friday, the yield on the benchmark 30-year bond backed up 16 points to 6.46 percent from 6.30 percent, due primarily to a stronger-than-expected National Association of Purchasing Management report.
The syndicate official added, "If you see (rate) levels get back to where they were, issuers might think we're hitting a psychological barrier, and start to do prefundings again."

High-grade deals expected for this week include: Staples Inc $200 million offering of 10-year debt (Baa3/BB-plus) via Goldman Sachs & Co; Meditrust Healthcare Inc $400 million multi-tranche debt (Baa3/BBB-minus) offering via Merrill Lynch & Co; Summit Properties $100 million debt (Baa3/BBB-minus) offering via JP Morgan Securities and Servicemaster LP $300 million two-part debt deal via JP Morgan.

First out of the shoot among high-yield issuers this week may be Alliance Gaming Corp with a 144a private placement of $125 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes via Credit Suisse First Boston.
Price talk on the debt offering (B3/B) is a spread of 375-400 basis points over comparable Treasuries, market sources said.
Alliance Gaming, which manufactures and operates gaming machines, will use the proceeds from the deal to redeem existing high-coupon debt and preferred stock.
Also for Monday, High Voltage Engineering Corp, a privately-held manufacturing conglomerate, is seen selling $120 million in seven-year 144a senior notes via CIBC Wood Gundy Corp.
Price talk on the deal (B3/B-plus) is 10.25-10.50 percent, market sources said.
